deep.reconstruction:
Context. The heading reads "Zu der Theorie der Fünftheilung gehören folgende Theoreme": these are lemmas for the quintisection, i.e. the order-5 transformation and modular equation worked on the previous page. Gauss's notation is:
- (x,y) = ∏_{n≥0}(1+x^{2n+1}y)(1+x^{2n+1}/y);
- [x] = ∏_{n≥1}(1−x^n).
By the Jacobi triple product (used implicitly, my remark), [x²]·(x,y) = θ(x,y) := Σ_{n∈Z} x^{n²} y^n.

[69] Ansatz. As a function of y, F(y) = (x,αy)(x,y/α) has the same quasi-periodicity under y→x²y as θ(x²,y²) and y·θ(x²,x²y²), and it is even under y→1/y. Gauss asserts
F(y) = P·S_e(y) + Q·S_o(y), with P, Q independent of y, where:
- S_e(y) = 1 + x²(y²+y⁻²) + x⁸(y⁴+y⁻⁴) + … = Σ x^{2n²} y^{2n} = θ(x²,y²);
- S_o(y) = y+1/y + x⁴(y³+y⁻³) + x¹²(y⁵+y⁻⁵) + … = Σ x^{2n(n+1)} y^{2n+1}.
The justification (two-dimensional space of such theta functions) is unstated. A margin note says one can also make the series multiplying P vanish, at y = ix (i.e. y² = −x²).

Determining P. Put y = i. Then (x,αi)(x,−αi) = ∏(1+x^{4n+2}α²)(1+x^{4n+2}/α²) = (x²,α²). Also S_o(i) = 0, and S_e(i) = 1 − 2x² + 2x⁸ − … = Σ(−1)^n x^{2n²} = [x²]²/[x⁴]. Hence P = (x²,α²)[x⁴]/[x²]².

Determining Q. Put y = −αx. Then y/α = −x, and the factor (1+x/y) of (x,−x) vanishes, so F = 0. Substituting gives:
- S_e(−αx) = Σ α^{2n} x^{2n(n+1)} = 1 + α⁻² + α²x⁴ + α⁻⁴x⁴ + …;
- S_o(−αx) = −(αx + 1/(αx) + x/α³ + α³x⁷ + x⁷/α⁵ + …).
Multiplying by α yields P·S_o(α) = (Q/x)·S_e(α). Using P = S_e(α)/[x²]² (since (x²,α²)[x⁴] = θ(x²,α²)), this gives Q = x·S_o(α)/[x²]².

(70) The result, in two forms:
- (x,αy)(x,y/α) = [x²]⁻² { S_e(α)S_e(y) + x·S_o(α)S_o(y) };
- equivalently, using S_o(y) = y·θ(x²,x²y²) = y[x⁴](x²,x²y²):
(x,αy)(x,y/α) = ([x⁴]²/[x²]²){ (x²,α²)(x²,y²) + xαy·(x²,α²x²)(x²,x²y²) }.

Side formulas (quasi-periodicity):
- (x,αx) = α⁻¹(x,x/α);
- (x,αx²) = (αx)⁻¹(x,α).
There is also an unclear scratch: −(y/x)(−x,−y).

(71) Dissection: (x,y) + (x,x/y)·(x/y²)^{1/4} = (x^{1/4},y^{1/2})·[x^{1/2}]/[x²]. Multiplied by [x²], this is Σ_k x^{k²/4}y^{k/2} split into even and odd k.

(72) Relabelling αy→α, y/α→β (so α²→α/β, y²→αβ):
(x,α)(x,β) = ([x⁴]²/[x²]²){ (x²,αβ)(x²,α/β) + xα(x²,αβx²)(x²,αx²/β) }.

Corollary. Replace α→x/α, β→x/β, then reduce with (x²,1/z) = (x²,z), (x²,zx⁴) = (zx²)⁻¹(x²,z) and (x²,zx²) = z⁻¹(x²,x²/z) (these reductions are mine). The result is
(x,x/α)(x,x/β) = ([x⁴]²/[x²]²){ (x²,x²/(αβ))(x²,α/β) + α(x²,αβ)(x²,αx²/β) }.
On the next page this is combined with (72) and (71) into [73], and used to prove the quintisection theorems.

In modern terms, (70)/(72) is the classical formula expressing a product of two theta functions by thetas of doubled nome, θ3(u)θ3(v) = θ3(u+v|2τ)θ3(u−v|2τ) + θ2(u+v|2τ)θ2(u−v|2τ).
errors: In the y=−αx substitution the first factor is written (x,−αx); it should be (x,−α²x), since αy = −α²x. This is harmless because the second factor (x,−x) is 0 anyway.
The two-term ansatz [69] is asserted without justification (that the space of such theta functions is two-dimensional); it is correct.
The series in (70) are left truncated ('…' omitted in the second bracket); this is cosmetic.
All final formulas (69)–(72), the side formulas and the corollary check out.

results.what: Product (x,αy)(x,y/α) expanded as P·θ(x²,y²) + Q·yθ(x²,x²y²), with P, Q found by specialising y=i and y=−αx
results.modern_name: Theta-function product/duplication formula θ3(u)θ3(v) = θ3(u+v|2τ)θ3(u−v|2τ) + θ2(u+v|2τ)θ2(u−v|2τ) (Watson-type addition formula)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (Fundamenta Nova 1829 and lectures 1835–38); in general form Riemann/Weierstrass

results.modern_name: 2-dissection of a theta series (even/odd index split)
Product formula for θ4 (Gauss's identity / triple product)

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's pre-Jacobi theta-function work, including product formulas and the order-5 transformation, is documented in Werke III/VIII and the literature (Schlesinger, Fricke, recent studies). This page is a clean, correct derivation of a standard theta product formula serving the quintisection. It is a nice dated detail, but not a new attribution.
